newsitem.title: THAILAND: Australian PM worsening racism row - Thai paper.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM worsening racism row - Thai paper.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard has deepened an anti-Asian row by not condemning racist statements made by a maverick politician, a Thai newspaper said on Thursday.
The Nation, responding to a letter from Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer, said in an editorial that Howard had scored "zero points" in the debate over anti-Asian sentiments in Australia.

Howard has been under fire in the Thai and some other Asian press this week for lashing at media criticism of his refusal to repudiate racist remarks made recently by Australian member of parliament Pauline Hanson.
In his letter, Downer had taken exception to the paper's editorial on Monday entitled "Howard's silence endorses Australia's racist fringe."
The minister said the editorial was inaccurate and offensive and he defended Howard's statements against racism, which have been general and not specifically aimed at Hanson or her comments.
But the Nation, which published Downer's letter on Thursday, replied that it had not at any time inferred that Australia was a racist and whites-only country.
The editorial said: "In terms of damage control to Australia's image, Howard scored zero points and has made matters only worse.

"The indisputable fact remains. Howard's failure to condemn Hanson by name, preferring to ignore her in the hope what she said would be conveniently forgotten in the rapidly changing political landscape, clearly backfired," it added.

Hanson, dumped from Howard's Liberal Party this year for controversial comments about aborigines, complained in her maiden parliamentary speech last month that Australia was being swamped by Asians and called for a halt to immigration.
The newspaper said Hanson had received a standing ovation at a meeting of the Australian National Party's women's branch in Queensland.
"The National Party is a junior partner in Howard's conservative coalition government. For us in Asia, this support for her views on race is frightening," the newspaper added.

Facing a mounting backlash from Asia and growing criticism at home over the race row, Howard on Wednesday accepted a Labor opposition proposal for a joint parliamentary motion condemning racism and pledging tolerance.

"This motion, it is about saying to the Australian people and saying to the nations of the region that we are a tolerant society, we are a compassionate society...," Howard said in moving the motion, which was carried by a large majority.
